g.text: Default GRU design: filtered retrieval + zero item initialization
Three GRU layers of 32 units | 128-unit prediction head | 215,233 parameters for the illustrated vocabularies
A Encode the inputs available before response t
Recency; item age; prior mean spacing
All item vectors START AT ZERO
Concatenate 16 time + 16 history + 16 item + 16 skill = 64 values
Input dropout 0.1 produces x(t), shared by retrieval, prediction and memory update
Recency = time since the previous response (any item). Item age and prior spacing use this student-item exposure history, including studies.
B Filter earlier memories, then retrieve: one head, width 32
Past completed events from this participant
Newest 100 globally: e(j): 96; post-answer h3(j): 32; raw item/skill IDs
FILTER: past item = current item OR past skill = current skill (compare raw IDs)
Zero weight on all other events
Weighted sum: Σ a(t,j) v(j), 32 values
Filter the last 100 global events, not the last 100 matches. Q/K share weights and bias; no attention decay or dropout.
The current answer is still unknown. Retrieved memory replaces the direct h3(t−1) input to this prediction head.
D Observe the answer, update all three GRU layers, then write the bank
Keep all three GRU states for the next trial
For the next trial: append [e(t): 96, new h3(t): 32, raw item/skill IDs]
Keep the newest 100 global events; e(t) is pre-answer, h3(t) is post-answer
All encoders, embeddings, GRU layers, retrieval projections and prediction weights learn jointly from response-prediction loss.
At a new participant: zero GRU states and an empty bank; keep the trained embeddings. Retrieval feeds prediction only.
Timing values use log(1 + seconds) and training-only scaling. Undefined prior spacing stays missing in the data, with an availability flag.
Only completed scored responses enter the bank. Dropout is off during evaluation. States and bank carry forward; gradients detach at 100-event BPTT chunk boundaries.
